skill.name: pts-pivotal-token-search
skill.description: Use PTS (Pivotal Token Search) to find the tokens, sentences and latent concepts that change whether a language model solves a task, read the resulting events file, explore it in the visualizer, and export it as datasets. Use when the user wants to analyze reasoning steps of a small local model, interpret a PTS events file, or plan a search.
skill.summary: Plan PTS searches, interpret reasoning events across three scales, and export local datasets with model-specific caveats.

content.user_title: Analyze Local Model Reasoning with PTS
content.value_statement: Reasoning traces do not show which events change a model's chance of solving a task. This skill guides PTS searches, event interpretation, and local dataset exports with explicit measurement caveats.
actual_capabilities: Check PTS availability and plan token or sentence searches around the selected model, dataset, device, and budget.
Guide optional Jacobian lens calibration and latent enrichment with shuffled controls.
Interpret JSONL event fields and rank token or sentence events by absolute probability change within one scale.
Explain model-specific results, heuristic event links, and limits on causal interpretation.
Guide hosted or local visualizer use while requiring permission before uploading private events.
Link events and export local datasets using documented formats, including DPO and steering.
limitations: PTS must already be installed; this skill does not install dependencies or provide the underlying implementation.
Searches require substantial sampling, and token or sentence scores depend on reliable answer checking.
Latent scores are observational and cannot be ranked directly against token or sentence probability changes.
Results depend on the model, task, and sampling settings; hosted-model analysis and general prompt tuning are outside scope.

use_cases.title: Investigate pivotal reasoning events
use_cases.description: Plan a small token or sentence search to identify events associated with changes in task success.

use_cases.title: Inspect a local evaluation trace
use_cases.description: Review existing event files, compare events within one scale, and identify examples that need manual checking.

use_cases.title: Prepare a local training dataset
use_cases.description: Link existing events and test a filtered DPO export before processing a larger collection.

prompt_templates.title: Understand an events file
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain the fields in my local PTS events file at [path]. Summarize its scales and model identifiers without running searches or uploading data.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a small search
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a token search for [model] on [dataset] using [device] within [budget]. Check available flags and ask before downloads or execution.

prompt_templates.title: Review latent evidence
prompt_templates.prompt: Review [events path] and plan J-lens enrichment for [model]. Include shuffled controls, consent for downloads, and separate reporting of latent scores.

prompt_templates.title: Design a controlled export workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Design repeated-seed checks and an intervention for [events path], then propose a filtered local DPO export. Separate observational findings from causal evidence.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: validate findings before dataset preparation

output_examples.input: Explain how to compare token events and latent events in my PTS file.
output_examples.output: Rank token events by absolute probability change and retain the direction of the shift. Report latent readout scores separately. Do not combine these scales into one ranking.

output_examples.input: Plan my first token search without starting it.
output_examples.output: Confirm the model, dataset, device, and time budget. Inspect the installed CLI flags. Propose fewer examples and samples for an initial pass. Request download consent and disclose the expected cost before execution.

output_examples.input: Prepare existing events for a local DPO export.
output_examples.output: Link the local events, inspect available export filters, and test DPO export on a small file. Review the sample before scaling up. Do not publish or upload the results.

best_practices: Confirm the model, dataset, device, budget, and download permissions before starting a small pilot search.
Compare events within one scale and model, inspect examples manually, and repeat measurements with other seeds.
Use shuffled controls for latent enrichment and require interventions before making causal claims.
anti_patterns: Do not combine latent readout scores and emitted-event probability shifts into one ranking.
Do not treat heuristic event links or category labels as verified causal mechanisms.
Do not install dependencies, download assets, or publish private events without the required user consent.

faq.question: Does this skill install PTS?
faq.answer: No. It checks the existing CLI and points to upstream installation documentation if PTS is missing.

faq.question: Which analysis scales does it cover?
faq.answer: It covers pivotal tokens, reasoning sentences called thought anchors, and latent concepts called meta-tokens.

faq.question: Can it analyze hosted models?
faq.answer: Hosted-model advice is outside scope. The workflow targets local models, and latent enrichment needs model-specific lens setup.

faq.question: Will my events be uploaded automatically?
faq.answer: No. The skill requires permission before hosted uploads and an explicit request before publishing through PTS commands.

faq.question: Do high scores prove a causal mechanism?
faq.answer: No. Scores have sampling noise, latent findings are observational, and links are heuristic. Repeat measurements and run interventions before causal claims.

faq.question: Which export formats are documented?
faq.answer: The skill lists causal_events, metatokens, pivotal_tokens, thought_anchors, dpo, and steering. Check installed CLI help and test a small local file first.
